title: Chapter 10: Landforms Created by Running Water (Fluvial Geomorphology)

blocks.content: Running water, which is considered the most important of all geomorphic agents, operates through two components: overland flow on the general land surface as a sheet and linear flow as streams and rivers in valleys.

rows: Removal of rock materials by hydraulic action and abrasion
Settling of transported sediments due to reduced river velocity
Alluvial Fans, Floodplains, Natural Levees, Oxbow Lakes, Deltas
High Kinetic Energy and steep stream gradient
Low Kinetic Energy and gentle stream gradient

items: Alluvial Fans are formed at the foot of mountain slopes due to sudden drop in gradient, whereas Deltas form at the river mouth.
Potholes form on river beds due to abrasion, while Plunge Pools form at the base of waterfalls due to hydraulic action.
Meanders are both erosional and depositional features, commonly asked in UPSC and State PSC exams regarding river stage identification.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Running water is the most dominant geomorphic agent shaping landscapes in humid climate regions.
Upper course (youthful stage) is characterized by steep gradients, dominant vertical erosion, and landforms like V-shaped valleys, gorges, and waterfalls.
Middle course (mature stage) sees dominant lateral erosion, forming wider floodplains, meanders, and alluvial fans.
Lower course (old stage) features slow-moving rivers, oxbow lakes, natural levees, and deltas near the river mouth.
